summary: This Microsoft Learn reference article documents the Transact-SQL date and time data types and functions used in SQL Server, Azure SQL Database, Azure SQL Managed Instance and Azure Synapse Analytics. It lists the six date/time data types with their formats, ranges, accuracy and storage sizes, and groups the functions into categories such as system date/time values, date parts, constructors from parts, differences, modifications, session format settings and validation. It also links to related articles on formatting, conversion, collations and time zone conversion.
one_line: Microsoft reference listing Transact-SQL date and time data types and functions across SQL Server and Azure SQL services.
key_facts: The Transact-SQL date and time data types are time, date, smalldatetime, datetime, datetime2 and datetimeoffset.
The datetime2 data type has a range of 0001-01-01 00:00:00.0000000 through 9999-12-31 23:59:59.9999999 with 100 nanoseconds accuracy and 6 to 8 bytes storage.
The smalldatetime data type has a range of 1900-01-01 through 2079-06-06 with 1 minute accuracy and 4 bytes storage.
The datetime data type has a range of 1753-01-01 through 9999-12-31 with 0.00333 second accuracy and 8 bytes storage.
The date data type covers 0001-01-01 through 9999-12-31 with 1 day accuracy and 3 bytes storage.
The datetimeoffset data type stores values in the format YYYY-MM-DD hh:mm:ss[.nnnnnnn] [+|-]hh:mm and uses 8 to 10 bytes of storage.
The time data type covers 00:00:00.0000000 through 23:59:59.9999999 and uses 3 to 5 bytes of storage.
The rowversion data type is not a date or time data type, and timestamp is a deprecated synonym for rowversion.
Since SQL Server 2008 (10.0.x), the Database Engine derives date and time values through the GetSystemTimeAsFileTime() Windows API, which has a precision fixed at 100 nanoseconds.
SYSDATETIME returns a datetime2(7) value, SYSDATETIMEOFFSET returns a datetimeoffset(7) value, and SYSUTCDATETIME returns a datetime2(7) value in UTC.
CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, GETDATE and GETUTCDATE return a datetime value and are classed as nondeterministic.
DATEDIFF returns an int and DATEDIFF_BIG returns a bigint for the number of datepart boundaries crossed between two dates.
SWITCHOFFSET changes the time zone offset of a DATETIMEOFFSET value and preserves the UTC value.
ISDATE determines whether a datetime or smalldatetime input expression has a valid date or time value.
